newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA inmates condemn Basque rebels for killing.
newsitem.headline: ETA inmates condemn Basque rebels for killing.

text.p: Three jailed ETA guerrillas condemned their Basque rebel comrades on Friday for killing a young politician, adding their voices to a national outcry against the radical separatists.
The three men read a statement at a Basque prison saying that, with the killing of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, ETA had "managed to accumulate more hate than in 38 years of terrorism."

Jose Manuel Soares Gamboa, Luis Gaston and Luis Gorriti, repentant members of the separatist group formed in 1959, also denounced ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna, saying every vote for the radical party was another bullet for ETA.

"After today, ETA has thousands of bullets fewer and this is good, it's the best thing that could happen to us," Soares Gamboa said, reading a statement to reporters at the Nanclares de Oca prison near the Basque capital Vitoria.
"I condemn ETA, I condemn Herri Batasuna, I condemn your crimes and your tortures."

Soares Gamboa, who was sentenced to more than 100 years in prison for involvement in a series of killings, turned himself in to Spanish authorities in 1994 and has since expressed regret in interviews and court appearances.
Gaston is awaiting trial on charges of belonging to an armed band and Gorriti has served three years of a 38-year sentence for various crimes.
With Spaniards already on edge and fearing fresh rebel violence, ETA was initially suspected of setting off a bomb which exploded at a Barcelona radio station on Friday.
But police said the blast, which caused minor damage but no injuries, apparently had no links to the guerrilla group. No one claimed responsibility for the bombing.
A Basque court upheld a Basque government decision to ban a planned pro-ETA rally for fear it would provoke a violent backlash at a time when anti-ETA emotions were running high.
Herri Batasuna, which had planned the rally for Saturday in the Basque city of San Sebastian, said it would abide by the court's ruling.
Scattered attacks have been made on Herri Batasuna supporters and offices since Blanco was killed, raising fears that ETA may retaliate.

Bells in churches and schools across Spain will ring out at 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Saturday, exactly one week after a deadline set by ETA for the government to transfer about 500 jailed comrades to prisons in the autonomous Basque region.
The goverment refused. Shortly after the deadline passed, ETA shot Blanco twice in the head and dumped him on the outskirts of San Sebastian. He died just before dawn on Sunday.
After the killed, an estimated six million people took to the streets in angry protests all over Spain.

Basques had long kept quiet out of fear of reprisals from the radical group, which has killed some 800 people in its struggle for an independent Basque state. But the massive protests awakened a new spirit of defiance.

Politicians who once would never have dared speak ill of ETA started proceedings on Friday to oust the Herri Batasuna mayor of Mondragon, a stronghold of diehard Basque nationalism. It was the first tangible move toward isolating the radical politicians.
